page: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor provides an extensive 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel AMX, AVX-512, and cryptographic hardware extensions.

The primary architectural distinction of the E16-4s_v6 is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio. It provides 128 GB of RAM across just 4 vCPUs, equating to 32 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators, requiring remote managed disks for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark evaluations show competitive single-threaded capabilities alongside expected multi-threaded constraints resulting from the 4-vCPU ceiling. Geekbench single-core performance registers at 2126 points, placing it in the top 25 percent, while multi-core scores reach 4801. Single-threaded throughput is further evidenced by a 31.33 GB/sec result in gzip compression and 2534 in Geekbench text processing. Conversely, aggregate multi-core tests reflect the low core count, with stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression falling into lower quartiles. Memory bandwidth measures 34.79 GB/sec for uncached reads and 24.77 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, this constrained-core VM format reduces software licensing fees tied directly to core counts while preserving a large memory footprint. The configuration is engineered for memory-intensive workloads that exhibit modest parallel computing demands, such as medium-scale caching nodes, in-memory databases, and memory-constrained analytical pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine offering 128 GB of RAM paired with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture, it features 2 physical cores, a 260 MB L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. The instance provides no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core reaching 2126 and gzip compression achieving 31.33 GB/sec, while multi-core metrics like stress-ng reflect the low thread count. Memory bandwidth clocks at 34.79 GB/sec for uncached reads. By offering 32 GB of RAM per vCPU, the E16-4s_v6 optimizes software licensing costs dependent on core counts, making it a targeted solution for in-memory databases, memory-heavy microservices, and specialized caching deployments.
